builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MAST: Medoid-Anchored Subspace Steering for Visual Grounding in Multimodal LLMs
summary: MAST replaces global-mean activation steering in multimodal LLMs with training-free, input-adaptive steering that routes each query to clustered task medoids and aggregates low-rank local directions; MAST-PR adds a lightweight probe to reweight task-specialized direction families. It costs offline clustering and medoid storage per task, plus per-query routing, subspace extraction, and optional probe inference, while adding pipeline complexity without reported latency or memory figures. It can fail if task clusters are unstable, routing mismatches queries, local low-rank directions do not transfer across models or datasets, or the probe introduces task-aware overfitting and serving fragility.
rationale: It is training-free and therefore compatible with constrained infrastructure, but the claim is task-specific and lacks baseline, latency, memory, and robustness evidence needed for production adoption without a small-scale validation on the reader's exact MLLM and visual-grounding workload.
technique: Medoid-anchored subspace activation steering for MLLMs

claims.statement: MAST replaces global-mean activation steering in multimodal LLMs with training-free, input-adaptive steering that routes each query to clustered task medoids and aggregates low-rank local directions; MAST-PR adds a lightweight probe to reweight task-specialized direction families. It costs offline clustering and medoid storage per task, plus per-query routing, subspace extraction, and optional probe inference, while adding pipeline complexity without reported latency or memory figures. It can fail if task clusters are unstable, routing mismatches queries, local low-rank directions do not transfer across models or datasets, or the probe introduces task-aware overfitting and serving fragility.
MAST-PR yields a further average improvement of +8.09 points over MAST on visual grounding; no absolute baseline, speed, or cost factor is reported.
